title: He lifts the ones the world forgot to notice
subtitle: Ar-Rafi': the One who raises believers in rank, honour and nearness to Him
intro: Ar-Rafi' (الرافع) means the Exalter, the One who raises: He lifts the believer in rank, the learner through knowledge, the humble in honour, and His servants by degrees in Paradise. It matters because your real standing is set by Him, not by followers, salary or family name, and anyone can climb.

root.sense: Raf' is to lift something up from below: raising a hand, raising a building, raising a voice. In Arabic grammar it names the case that lifts a word's ending. The picture is of being carried upward out of a low place by someone stronger than you.

knowing: Ar-Rafi' is the One who raises. He lifts people in their standing, their knowledge, their reputation and, above all, in their nearness to Him. The Quran says that Allah raises those who believe and those given knowledge by degrees (58:11), and after Ibrahim's argument with his people: We raise by degrees whom We will (6:83). The name is in the well-known list in Jami' al-Tirmidhi, and scholars mention it together with Al-Khafid, the One who lowers.

{idea}His raising is real raising.{/idea} People can put you on a stage, but they cannot put you in a high place in His sight, and the one He raises no one can pull down. He raised the mention of the Prophet ﷺ (94:4), so that his name is called out in the adhan somewhere on earth at every moment of the day.

His measure is different from ours. The most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most mindful of Him (49:13). Not lineage, not looks, not degrees, not the size of the house. That is what makes this name such a mercy: the ladder He offers is open to the poor, the unknown and the overlooked as much as to anyone.
seeing: Bilal ibn Rabah was enslaved, mocked and tortured on burning sand. Then the Prophet ﷺ told him that he had heard Bilal's footsteps ahead of him in Paradise, and Bilal could only think of one habit: he prayed whenever he made wudu (Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim). Two quiet prayers, done sincerely, lifted a man the world had trampled.

Julaybib was a companion whom people overlooked. When he was killed in battle, the Prophet ﷺ searched for him, stood over him and said he is from me and I am from him (Sahih Muslim). People had not ranked him; Allah had.

Yusuf was thrown into a well, sold cheaply and imprisoned. In the end he raised his parents up onto the throne of Egypt (12:100). Ar-Rafi' had been lifting him the whole time, even in the dark years when it looked like falling.
trusting: If you feel invisible, like the carer nobody thanks or the worker passed over again, remember that the leaderboard that matters is His. You might be last in people's eyes and first in His. {reward}A sincere act no one sees can lift you higher than a whole career.{/reward}

So stop chasing being raised by people. Viral posts, the right contacts, the right brands: these give a height that can vanish overnight. {trap}Status sought from people turns you into their prisoner.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ said that no one humbles himself for Allah except that Allah raises him (Sahih Muslim). The way up runs through prostration.
loving: We love the one who picks us up when we have fallen, who notices us in a crowded room. Allah does not only raise those who are already high. He lifted a freed slave to the roof of the Ka'bah to call the adhan, a prisoner to the palace, and He lifts the sinner who returns, sometimes higher than before he fell. {idea}Knowing that He is watching to lift you makes the heart run towards Him.{/idea}
now: You open LinkedIn and see an old classmate announce yet another promotion, while you are on the night shift caring for your mother. It feels like you are falling behind. Ar-Rafi' keeps a different record, and every hour of that shift is being lifted to Him. Put the phone down and make one sincere dua for your classmate too.
old: I measure how high I am by my title, my income and how other people see me.
new: My real rank is whatever Allah raises, and He lifts the humble and the sincere whether anyone notices or not.
try: Pray two rak'ahs after your next wudu, as Bilal did, and tell no one about it.

dua.text: Ya Rafi', raise me in Your sight, not in the eyes of people. Lift my heart above what is low, raise my rank through faith and knowledge, and raise my parents and loved ones in Paradise.
dua.note: Call on Him by this name when you feel overlooked or are tempted to chase status, remembering that the one He raises cannot be brought down.

pairs.why: He raises and He lowers: one scale of justice in His hand, so the two names are said together.
Ar-Rafi' lifts rank and degree; Al-Mu'izz gives honour and strength. Both come from Him alone.

faq.a: Ar-Rafi' means the Exalter, the One who raises. Allah lifts believers by degrees, raises those given knowledge, honours the humble, and raises His servants in Paradise. The name is in the well-known list in Jami' al-Tirmidhi and is mentioned together with Al-Khafid, the One who lowers.

faq.q: What is the difference between Ar-Rafi' and Al-Mu'izz?
faq.a: The two are close. Ar-Rafi' focuses on lifting in rank and degree, such as raising believers and scholars by degrees (58:11). Al-Mu'izz focuses on granting honour, dignity and strength (3:26). Both teach that real standing comes only from Allah.

faq.q: How does Allah raise a person?
faq.a: The Quran ties raising to faith and knowledge (58:11) and to mindfulness of Allah (49:13). The Prophet ﷺ said that no one humbles himself for Allah except that Allah raises him (Sahih Muslim). Sincere worship, beneficial knowledge and humility are the paths He opens.
